title: Progressive traffic choreography and auto-recovery lattice
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Background: As we scale LTS channels and support mixed hosted/dedicated/private deployments, our current canary and percentage-ramp tooling is brittle for multi-variant releases (model + runtime changes). We need a cohesive controller that composes per-release policies (version pins, LTS channel membership), feature-flag signal weaving, and an auto-recovery lattice that will orchestrate gradual ramps, apply safety checks, and perform scored automatic rollbacks when necessary. Goals: 1) Provide deterministic, auditable ramps for releases that can span models, runtime revisions, and quantized variants. 2) Implement a recovery/rollback scorer that considers error-rate, latency regressions, quality regressions (eval sets/prompts), and cost regressions. 3) Expose canary progress and manual override controls in Console and the CLI. 4) Support staged promotion across LTS channels (canary -> beta -> stable) with configurable traffic curves and hold windows. Constraints: must integrate with existing routing layer (traffic-proxy and route-controller), respect Dedicated capacity overrides, and run in air-gapped Private installs with minimal external dependency. Privacy/security: rollout decisions are control-plane only; no customer prompt data is persisted outside current audit streams.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can execute a configured percentage ramp (0->100) with configurable steps and hold windows via API and Console

Rollback scorer triggers automatic rollback when any high-priority rule fires (e.g., absolute 5xx increase >0.5% or 2x baseline, p99 latency regression >200ms absolute or >50% relative, eval-quality drop >3% measured on canonical prompt set)
Canary and shadow traffic modes available; shadow mode must route copies to candidate variant without affecting production counters
Traffic choreography supports heterogenous release bundles (model+runtime+quant) and falls back to compatible variant when unavailable
Integration tests simulate degraded DB/infra and validate safe-halting and recovery behavior
Console shows live progress, health signals, and a one-click abort/promote button with audit entry
Playbook and runbook documented with step-by-step manual recovery and escalation paths
tasks: Design rollout policy DSL and YAML schema (include threshold rules, cohort definitions, hold windows, and scoring weights)
Implement rollout-controller service changes: policy engine, adaptive ramp executor, and rollback scorer
Add traffic escrow token to route-controller to enable distributed shutdown of cohorts
Wire telemetry hooks: per-release counters, delta baselining, and quality-eval ingest pipeline
Console UI: progress timeline, health indicators, override modal, and audit log entries
Add CLI commands: redwood rollout start|status|abort|promote with JSON policy input
Create staging runs on dedicated GPU pool and run two full smoke cycles with synthetic traffic
Author regression tests (unit/integration/e2e) and update CI to gate rollout-controller PRs
Write runbook and SLA escalation matrix and run a tabletop exercise with oncall and SRE
